clue.text: Illustration perfectionist end-lessly revised

indicators.note: without its end means the final letter of the word before is dropped
a revised text has been reworked, so the remaining letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, before losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A fussy illustrator keeps reworking a picture without ever finishing it.
explanation.walkthrough: PERFECTIONIST minus its final T leaves twelve letters, which rearrange to FRONTISPIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontispiece is the decorative picture facing a book's title page, a specific kind of illustration.

clue.text: Note number is even

definitions.note: a verb here: to even something out

blocks.note: a flat is a musical note lowered by a semitone
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A musician remarks that a certain note's number is an even one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adjective about the number, but it is a verb meaning to make level.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatten a surface is to make it level and smooth, which is one sense of the verb to even.

clue.text: Upstart in deep South said to go round the world

definitions.text: said to go round the world

indicators.note: one piece placed in another means it sits inside the following letters

blocks.note: the start of the word up
the deep is a poetic name for the sea
S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: Some brash newcomer in the American South is rumoured to be travelling round the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstart' splits into 'up' and 'start': the start of 'up' is U.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Oceanus was the Titan personifying the great river believed to encircle the whole flat earth.

clue.text: Plant takes a Spanish wine ...

blocks.note: tarragon is a herb used in cooking
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plant draws up a Spanish wine, perhaps fed to it by a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries 'Spanish wine' on into the next clue, 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragona is a Catalan port whose surrounding region gives its name to a sweet, strong Spanish wine.

clue.text: ... and gets rid of others

definitions.note: short for other Spanish wines, carried over from 3 down

blocks.note: first meaning: further Spanish wines, since sack was a dry white wine from Spain
second meaning: dismisses from a job

explanation.surface: Read with 3 down, a plant drinks one Spanish wine and throws the rest away.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack is the old name for sherry-type wines from Spain, Falstaff's favourite drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack was a dry Spanish wine, so other such wines are sacks; to sack someone is also to fire them from a job.

clue.text: Maintain vital air supply at top of church

blocks.note: at a place is in it
a spire is the pointed top of a church tower

explanation.surface: Someone up a church steeple keeps the breath of life going.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the literal sense of the answer: breathing in.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire is literally to breathe in, drawing in the air that keeps a body alive.

clue.text: This head doesn't find it easy to lie

definitions.text: This head doesn't find it easy to lie

blocks.clueFragment: This head doesn't find it easy to lie
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who is a poor liar, or cannot get comfortable on the pillow
setter's reading: Shakespeare's 'Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown', from Henry IV Part 2

explanation.surface: An honest person, or an insomniac, struggles to lie.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is King Henry IV lamenting that a monarch cannot sleep easily.
explanation.definitionFit: A head that wears a crown belongs to a monarch, and Shakespeare says such a head lies uneasily.

clue.text: How a conductor should take what's coming to him

blocks.note: setter's reading: a conductor stands facing the orchestra and the score
surface reading: accept punishment or consequences

explanation.surface: Advice on how a conductor ought to accept whatever is heading his way.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means accepting the consequences of one's actions; a conductor does it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to confront unpleasant consequences bravely, accepting deserved criticism or punishment.

clue.text: No profit from this sort of play ... (7) unseen actors abandoned

not part of this clue: the scan merged in the text of 9 across

explanation.walkthrough: The scanned text runs this clue into the next one; only the words up to the ellipsis belong here.

clue.text: Commander gives some land to shepherd

blocks.note: a field is a piece of land

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shepherd' looks like a noun receiving the land, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A field marshal is the highest army rank, so such an officer commands entire armies.

clue.text: Rebuilt on a site in country

indicators.note: something rebuilt has been put together again in a different form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A building is reconstructed on a plot somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In country' reads as rural, but country is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic nation, independent again since 1991 and bordered by Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Skill of expert, since converted to church

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An expert's know-how has since been turned to the service of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' suggests religious conversion, sitting next to 'church'.

explanation.surface: Someone gains an advantage by slightly shady means.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned text puts 12 across's clue in front of this one; the clue begins at 'Gives'. 'Edge' sounds like advantage but means a sharp blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To hone a knife is to sharpen it on a whetstone, literally giving the blade a keen edge.

clue.text: Golfing event finished without determination

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: lacking any fixed limit

blocks.note: the Open is golf's major tournament
finished means came to an end

explanation.surface: A golf tournament ended with the players lacking resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Determination' suggests grit, but here it means being settled or fixed in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-ended has no predetermined limit or conclusion, so it is undetermined.

clue.text: Vigorous development eg in Crete

indicators.note: development turns something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An example of vigorous building development on the island of Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone energetic is full of energy and strength, acting forcefully and with plenty of vigour.

clue.text: Eccentric character means to proceed on foot at two speeds

blocks.note: to march is to walk at a steady pace
the second speed: to hare is to run very fast

explanation.surface: An odd character explains how to walk with two different paces.
explanation.walkthrough: The two verbs give the two speeds: a steady walk, then a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: The March Hare is the mad host of the tea party in Alice in Wonderland, a famously eccentric figure.

clue.text: Result of appeal in second Test?

definitions.text: Result of appeal in second Test?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cricket appeal for a wicket during the second Test match

explanation.surface: A cricketer appeals during the second Test match, and we ask what comes of it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a Test is an international match, and fielders appeal to the umpire for a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: A court of appeal may order a case to be tried again before a new jury.

clue.text: Utterly unreliable evidence

blocks.note: surface reading: completely untrustworthy
setter's reading: by way of what was uttered, passed on by word of mouth

explanation.surface: A lawyer dismisses some testimony as completely untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' is read as 'by utterance', not 'totally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is testimony about what someone else said, which courts treat as unreliable second-hand information.

clue.text: Run into vulgar parents in Italian city

indicators.note: to run into something here means to be placed inside it

blocks.note: pa and ma are informal names for father and mother
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A traveller bumps into embarrassing parents while visiting an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar' signals the colloquial forms of the words for parents.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a city in northern Italy, famous for its ham and Parmesan cheese.

clue.text: 4 Could be an instrument in making his joke

clue.text: What are those revolting people getting up to?

definitions.text: What are those revolting people getting up to?

clue.text: TV's having trouble. 9 after Blue Peter's showing

clue.text: Communist makes his comeback in Nine Lives

clue.text: First book is on DNA units

clue.text: "Now sleeps the — petal, now the white" (Tennyson)
